title: Introduce pluggable retry adapters and per-consumer load-shedding for async workers
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last year we've accrued several pragmatic fixes to Redis/Kafka worker behavior — ad-hoc retry counters, duplicated backpressure checks, and a couple of consumer-specific rate limiters hard-coded into service logic. This has made cross-team changes risky and contributed to regressions during peak bursts (e.g., 2025-11-07 incident where cascading requeues amplified load).

Goal: Refactor the async consumer layer to: (1) extract retry logic into pluggable adapters (exponential/backoff/linear/custom hooks), (2) centralize load-shedding via a per-consumer-group token-bucket limiter and configurable shedding policies, and (3) unify observability and metrics so we can target regressions reliably. The end state should allow product teams to opt into different retry strategies without touching business code and let ops tune shedding thresholds per route or tenant.

Scope: Redis stream consumers and Kafka consumers across inference-dispatch, event-fanout, and batch-postprocess pipelines. NOT in scope: HTTP frontend rate-limiting (handled separately) and on-prem dedicated agents (follow-up ticket).

Design summary: - Runtime will expose a ConsumerMiddleware chain. Middleware types: RetryAdapter (pluggable), BackpressurePolicy (token-bucket limiter + overload detector), DLQPolicy (dead-letter / requeue windows). - RetryAdapter interface supports: maxAttempts, backoffStrategy, jitter, conditional predicates (isRetryable(error, msg)). We'll implement: exponential-jitter (default), linear, and a no-retry adapter. - Backpressure: per-consumer token-bucket with shared burst allowance and a soft/hard threshold. Soft threshold starts shedding low-priority messages (ack with drop metric); hard threshold rejects/leases messages back with a Retry-After. Policy configurable via config service + runtime API. - Redis changes: migrate legacy pop/ack loop to consumer-group based lease+extend model; use a leader election window for reclaimer to avoid hot reclaims. - Kafka changes: adjust commit semantics to commit after successful handler; support pause/resume with dynamic pause window when backlog grows. - Observability: emit retry_count, retry_strategy, shed_reason, token_bucket_fill, lease_reclaims, dlq_enqueue for each message id (trace id). Add per-route dashboards and alerting thresholds (DLQ rate > 0.5% 10m, shed_rate > 2% 5m).

Migration plan: 1) Build middleware API and unit tests behind feature flag (runtime-1.21). 2) Implement adapters and token-bucket limiter as library in infra/common-consumer. 3) Canary deploy to low-traffic pipelines (batch-postprocess) for 48 hours with strict telemetry. 4) Gradually enable for inference-dispatch in heavy-read replica with 1% traffic then 10% then 100%. 5) Rollback plan: feature flag toggle and automated rollback if DLQ rate or latency deviate beyond thresholds.

Success metrics: - Reduce cascade requeues during bursts (DLQ rate drop target: >30% reduction from baseline) - Reduce CPU spikes caused by tight retry loops (target 15% lower 95th CPU) - Clearer alerting (false positive SLO alert reduction by 40%)

Risks and trade-offs: - Introducing middleware adds indirection; careful benchmarking required to keep per-message overhead minimal (~<1ms). - Token-bucket tuning may require several iterations and per-tenant defaults. - If misconfigured, shedding can cause QPS loss; we mitigate this via conservative defaults and canarying.

Related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-33542+Consumer+Middleware+Design (draft), Perf benchmark notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/benchmarks/consumer-mw-2026, RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/112
comments:
2026-02-26 - Initial spike: prototyped middleware chain and a simple exponential adapter. Discovered legacy Redis consumer relies on redis-legacy pop pattern; converting to XGROUP will require changing message IDs stored in tracing.
2026-03-03 - Design review: PM and SRE reviewed. SRE requested per-tenant default policies and an emergency global shedding kill-switch. Added to design.
2026-03-08 - Implementation: adapter interfaces implemented in infra/common-consumer; unit tests + fakes added. Local bench: overhead ~0.6ms per message on dev machine with default adapter.
2026-03-11 - PR opened for Redis consumer migration (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-consumers/pull/387. Need to coordinate migration with batch-postprocess owner @Lina.
2026-03-12 - SRE requested additional metric: token_bucket_fill_percent exposed as prometheus gauge and an alert runbook. Added to PR.
